title: Balanced and unbalanced forces (বলের সাম্যাবস্থা ও অসাম্যাবস্থা)
placement: Book pages 69–70, topic 3.3: বলের সাম্যাবস্থা ও অসাম্যাবস্থা (Balanced and Unbalanced Forces). Next to চিত্র ৩.০২ (a ball hanging on a string; the same pendulum pulled aside) and চিত্র ৩.০৩ (a heavy book hung from a rope pulled at both ends).
description: Interactive 3D figure for balanced and unbalanced forces (বলের সাম্যাবস্থা ও অসাম্যাবস্থা), book pages 69–70, topic 3.3: the page's two pictures, real size. চিত্র ৩.০২: a 1 kg steel ball hangs on a 30 cm cord from the hook of a lab stand; the pull of the cord T (orange) and the weight W = 9.8 N (violet) are equal and opposite, the resultant is zero (সাম্যাবস্থা). The student pulls the ball aside: a hand pinches it and pulls too (light orange, at right angles to the cord), and the three forces cancel. Let go: the hand's pull is gone, T and W no longer cancel, their resultant (black, mg sin θ) acts and the ball swings in real time (the forces stay correct throughout: T = mg cos θ + mLω²). Or, while it hangs still, the student cuts the cord (tap it, or the button): T is gone, only W is left, the অসাম্য বল; the ball falls with g onto the bench, five times slower, leaving a mark every 0.04 s (the gaps grow), the view following it down; on the bench its push balances W again. চিত্র ৩.০৩: a heavy book hangs from the middle of a rope whose ends two hands pull; T₁, T₂ and W add up to zero at every angle; dragging the hands apart makes the pulls grow (T = W / 2 sin α) while the book stays at rest. Every change takes a force away or adds one. The panel names the state in the book's words and draws the forces tip to tail: the chain closes when the resultant is zero. Forces in নিউটন (N). Test: 5 questions (the pull of a string holding a body at rest, read off the picture; which force is unbalanced after the cut; which of four arrows is the resultant just after letting go; what the book's two pulls add up to; what pulling the rope tighter does). Phone-first, Bangla.
